ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle EDC$, where point D is on $AB$, and $\angle B=60^\circ$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle EDA$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle EDC$,\\
it follows that $\angle B = \angle EDC = 60^\circ$, $CD = CB$,\\
hence $\angle CDB = \angle B = 60^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle EDA = 180^\circ - \angle EDC - \angle CDB = \boxed{60^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Figure description: in the figure, A, D, B are on the same horizontal straight line, and D is between A and B; C is above the base and slightly to the right, and E is at the upper left. The figure has segments AC, BC, CD, EC, ED, etc. drawn, triangles ABC and EDC share vertex C, and the problem gives that they are congruent. Reasoning: from the ordered congruence relation \(\triangle ABC \cong \triangle EDC\), the corresponding vertices are \(A\leftrightarrow E\), \(B\leftrightarrow D\), \(C\leftrightarrow C\). Therefore \(\angle B = \angle EDC = 60^\circ\), and the corresponding side \(CB = CD\). Because D is on AB, viewed from B, ray BD and BA are in the same direction, so \(\angle CBD = \angle CBA = \angle B = 60^\circ\). Also because \(CB = CD\), triangle CDB is an isosceles triangle, so \(\angle CDB = \angle CBD = 60^\circ\). At point D, DA and DB form a straight line, and the sum of the three adjacent angles above, \(\angle EDA\), \(\angle EDC\), and \(\angle CDB\), is \(180^\circ\). So \(\angle EDA = 180^\circ - 60^\circ - 60^\circ = 60^\circ\).
